# Maximum Value of an Ordered Triplet I.

@example The best triple takes 8, then 2, then 6: (8 - 2) * 6 = 36.
[8,3,5,2,6]
=> 36

@example The values only grow, so nums[i] - nums[j] is below zero in every triple, and so is every value: the answer is 0.
[3,7,8,20]
=> 0

@example The only triple is (5 - 5) * 7 = 0.
[5,5,7]
=> 0

# Three elements, one positive triple.
[10,1,3]
=> 27

# Values at the bounds: 999999 * 10^6 needs more than 32 bits.
[1000000,1,1000000]
=> 999999000000

# Strictly increasing: every triple is negative.
[1,2,3,4,5]
=> 0

# All equal: every triple is 0.
[6,6,6,6]
=> 0

# The largest element is too early to be nums[k]: (100 - 1) * 2.
[3,100,1,2]
=> 198

# The best nums[i] is not next to nums[j]: (9 - 2) * 7.
[9,2,7,1,4]
=> 49

# Strictly decreasing: (5 - 3) * 2 beats (5 - 4) * 3 and (5 - 2) * 1.
[5,4,3,2,1]
=> 4

# Two close choices of j: (10^6 - 1) * 999999 beats (10^6 - 2) * 999999.
[1000000,1,2,999999]
=> 999998000001

# The largest difference is not the best: (10 - 5) * 100 beats
# (100 - 1) * 2.
[10,5,100,1,2]
=> 500

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[4,3,1,5,5]
=> 15

@gen 2 small
[4,2,5,2,4,1,3]
=> 12

@gen 3 small
[6,5,2,3,4,5,7,2]
=> 28

@gen 4 small
[1,9,2,5]
=> 35

@gen 5 small
[834022,695643,874140,482840,186695,732374]
=> 503466844430

@gen 6 small
[3,1,8,9,6,4]
=> 18
